Embed

im-BED -- two syllables, stress on the second syllable, BED. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To embed to fix firmly into something.

Engineers embed sensors deep in the dam's walls to track the slightest movement.

Worked Example

At midnight, the road crew pours fresh asphalt and presses a line of glass reflectors into it, one every few feet. By morning the surface has hardened around each one, and no storm or snowplow will pry them loose.

The crew embedded the reflectors: fixed them firmly INTO the road so they became part of it. Embed always involves a surrounding material that closes around the object -- and it works figuratively too, as when a melody embeds itself in your memory.

How Embed Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

lodge

lodge: to make something stick firmly in a place

implant

implant: to insert or fix something deeply into something else

Antonyms

dislodge

dislodge: to knock something out of its fixed place

remove

remove: to take something away from where it is

How Strong Is It? — lodge → embed → implant

lodge vs. embed

lodge vs. embed: Lodge can happen by accident -- a pebble lodges in a boot -- while embed usually means someone deliberately fixes a thing into a material so it stays.

implant vs. embed

implant vs. embed: Implant is the strongest and deepest: an embedded stone sits firmly in the ring's band, but an implanted device is set INSIDE a living thing, meant to become a working part of it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — em-

prefix — em-: in, into (Latin in-, via French en-)

root — bed

root — bed: a resting place, a base (Old English bedd)

Put it together

Put it together: Embed is literally 'to put into a bed' -- em- ('into') plus bed. Picture a jewel pressed into a bed of gold, or a fossil lying in its bed of stone: to embed something is to tuck it into a material that holds it fast.

Use the root in a new word: bedrock

Use the root in a new word: bedrock: The bridge's pillars are anchored in solid bedrock far below the riverbed.

Root Check

Word Choice

Embed takes IN or INTO plus a surrounding material: embed posts in concrete, embed a chip into a card. The figurative uses keep the same picture -- a reporter embedded with a unit travels inside it, and a habit embedded in a routine is fixed so firmly it feels built in.
